items.title: Ramsey Lewis — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

ctx.x: assumption – you mentioned Sonny. Maybe that’s Sonny Boy Williamson, working the stockroom. So I don’t know. But perhaps you just shared . . .

I think that Daddy-O Daylie – Holmes Daylie was his name. His personality, his radio name, was Daddy-O. He was an advantage to us in many ways. Our business with the Chess people, fortunately Daddy-O, not that he was our business representative, but he would always say, “Make sure you” and then he’d fill in the blank. “Now when you do the” – “make sure” – it was always “make sure.” I learned early on that I’d rather have a royalty statement than a Cadillac. I learned early on that I’d rather have a royalty…
That’s good. I wasn’t looking for a horror story. I just wanted to know what your relationship was, given the longevity of your . . .
